page: Google Cloud Platform c4-standard-96-lssd is a compute-optimized server configured with 96 vCPUs and 360 GB of RAM. Powered by an Intel Xeon 6985P-C processor running at 2.3 GHz, this instance features 48 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The CPU architecture is x86_64, supported by a 504 MB L3 cache. It includes 6167 GB of local NVMe SSD storage distributed across 16 local SSDs, with no integrated GPU.

Benchmark results indicate strong multi-core performance, with stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core scores placing in the top 25%. The system excels in memory bandwidth, achieving top-tier status for small-block cached reads at 7717.61 GB/sec. It also demonstrates top-tier performance in Passmark database operations, Redis SET operations at 171.76 million operations per second, and static web serving throughput at 150.43 GB/sec. Advanced instruction sets like AVX-512 and Intel AMX contribute to top-tier scores in extended instructions, cryptography, and software compilation.

From a resource-density perspective, the combination of high-count dedicated vCPUs and massive local NVMe SSD storage provides high qualitative cost efficiency for IOPS-heavy and compute-intensive workloads. The lack of a GPU limits its suitability for heavy model training, but its AMX support enables strong performance in CPU-based LLM inference, particularly for prompt processing. This server is highly suited for large-scale database hosting, high-throughput web serving, software compilation pipelines, and intensive data-processing tasks.
